battle.name: 利蘭丁戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前710年前後，埃維厄島上卡爾基斯與埃雷特里亞為爭奪利蘭丁平原開戰，打了數十年，數度休戰，米利都、薩摩斯與色薩利等盟友亦被捲入。修昔底德稱這是特洛伊戰爭之後唯一一場同盟城邦合力交鋒的戰爭。戰陣以劍兵為主、禁用弓與投石器，卡面這支斯巴達長矛所代表的矛兵，仍是重裝步兵的標準配備。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 利蘭丁戰爭是古風時期希臘城邦之間最長久的一場戰爭，交戰雙方是埃維厄島西岸的兩座伊奧尼亞城邦：北面的卡爾基斯與南面的埃雷特里亞。卡爾基斯扼守島上最狹窄處的歐里波斯海峽，海陸商路必經，境內出產銅鐵，盛產陶器與葡萄；埃雷特里亞則控制島上約四分之一的土地，勢力遠及基克拉澤斯群島的安德羅斯、蒂諾斯與凱亞，其母邦聚落列夫坎迪的遺址至今仍可見。軍隊方面，埃雷特里亞在國勢頂峰可撥出約三千名重裝步兵、六百名騎兵與六十輛戰車，顯示它正站在荷馬式貴族作戰向城邦重裝步兵過渡的門檻上；卡爾基斯的兵員數目已無從考證，只知其步兵精於對手而騎兵明顯不足。指揮體系仍是城邦公民軍：各支隊伍由抽籤或選任的執政官率領，沒有常設總司令，也沒有流傳下來的同盟條約文本。埃雷特里亞一方有米利都支持，戰爭中米利都曾出兵掃蕩島南端的卡里斯托斯；卡爾基斯一方則有薩摩斯與色薩利加入，埃伊達、科林斯、梅加拉，甚至希俄斯與厄立特里亞亦被學者推測站在同一邊。整場戰爭本質上是城邦聯盟式的對決，雙方都要靠盟邦提供的步兵、騎兵或船隊撐住戰線。
countriesEn: The Lelantine War was the longest of the wars fought between the Greek city-states of the Archaic period. The belligerents were two Ionian poleis on the western side of Euboea: Chalcis in the north and Eretria in the south. Chalcis commanded the narrowest crossing of the island, the Euripus strait, through which every sea and land route passed; the region was famous for its copper and iron, for its pottery and for its vineyards. Eretria controlled roughly a quarter of the island and extended its sway to the Cycladic islands of Andros, Tenos and Kea, and the site of its mother settlement at Lefkandi is still traceable. On the military side, at the height of its power Eretria could muster about 3,000 hoplites, 600 cavalrymen and 60 chariots, which places it on the threshold between the aristocratic warfare of Homer and the citizen hoplite army of the polis; the numbers of Chalcis are unknown, though its infantry was better than its rival's and its cavalry decidedly weaker. Command remained that of the citizen militia: each contingent was led by archons chosen by lot or by election, there was no permanent commander-in-chief, and no treaty of alliance has survived. Eretria was supported by Miletus, which during the war ravaged Karystos in the south of the island; Chalcis could count on Samos and Thessaly, while Aegina, Corinth, Megara and possibly Chios and Erythrai are thought by scholars to have stood on the same side. In essence the war was a contest between coalitions of city-states, each side needing the infantry, cavalry or fleets of its allies to hold the line.
people: 利蘭丁戰爭沒有留下成篇的指揮官傳記，能點名的人物多來自百年之後的零星記載。最重要者是色薩利佛薩羅斯的貴族克利奧馬科斯：據普魯塔克《道德論集》，埃雷特里亞的騎兵在平原上壓倒卡爾基斯步兵之後，他率色薩利騎隊解圍，衝入敵陣最密集處把對手擊潰，隨後自己也戰死陣中；卡爾基斯公民為他在市集豎立紀念柱，柱身據說直到普魯塔克時代仍在。另一位是卡爾基斯貴族安斐達馬斯，據傳在爭奪利蘭丁平原的戰鬥中陣亡，葬禮競技會上傳出荷馬與赫西俄德比拚詩技的說法，赫西俄德本人也在《工作與時日》中提到這場為安斐達馬斯舉辦的競技。城邦層面的推手則是雙方的執政官團：傳統還留下一條嚴厲的城邦法令，凡殺死本城名將者一律處死，阿基洛科斯詩中「歐玻亞的戰士們熟悉這樣的戰法」一句，正是這類習慣的見證。修昔底德在《伯羅奔尼撒斯戰爭史》開篇追述前代戰爭時，把這場戰爭列為特洛伊戰爭與波斯戰爭之間唯一有同盟參與者的大戰，實際上成了他的斷代標尺。希羅多德在第五卷又補記：公元前494年埃雷特里亞之所以派兵援助米利都，正是因為米利都曾在對卡爾基斯的戰爭中站在埃雷特里亞一方，薩摩斯則站在對面。
peopleEn: The Lelantine War left no full-length biographies of its generals, and the individuals who can be named come down to scattered notes written a century or more later. The most important of them is Cleomachus, an aristocrat of Pharsalus in Thessaly: according to Plutarch in the Moralia, after the Eretrian horse had overrun the Chalcidian foot, he led the Thessalian cavalry to the rescue, charged into the thickest of the enemy and routed them, and was himself slain in the fighting; the Chalcidians raised a commemorative column for him in the agora, and the pillar was said to be standing there in Plutarch's own day. The second figure is Amphidamas, a Chalcidian nobleman who is said to have fallen in one of the battles fought over the Lelantine plain; the funeral games held for him carried the story that Homer and Hesiod matched verses there, and Hesiod himself mentions the games of Amphidamas in the Works and Days. At the level of the city-states the driving forces were the boards of archons on both sides: Chalcis is said by tradition to have had a law ordering the execution of anyone who killed their champion, and the line in Archilochus about the warlike lords of Euboea being experienced in that manner of fighting is testimony to habits of this kind. Thucydides, opening the History of the Peloponnesian War with a survey of earlier Greek history, lists this war as the only one between the Trojan War and the Persian Wars fought with allied contingents, and it effectively became his chronological landmark. Herodotus adds in Book V that Eretria sent troops to help Miletus in 494 BC precisely because Miletus had stood on Eretria's side in the war against Chalcis, while Samos had taken the opposite side.
kits: 本卡的主兵器是斯巴達長矛，即古希臘重裝步兵的標準長矛，約兩米長，槍杆為木，槍尾裝有銅套。它不是某支特種部隊的專用配備，而是整個古風時期希臘步兵的公共裝備：一端是金屬矛刃，另一端可插地支撐盾面，讓密集的矛陣在對撞時互相頂住。但利蘭丁戰爭的年代正卡在裝備轉型的關口，這一點在文獻中看得很清楚。亞基洛科斯的詩說，決戰之日「弓不必張開，投石器也不會常見，讓人嘆息的活兒全歸劍去做」，歐玻亞的貴族們熟悉的是這樣的戰法；斯特拉波則記載兩城在爭端初起時曾約定交戰條件，特別禁止使用遠程投射武器，埃雷特里亞阿馬林提翁的某根石柱上至今刻著這條禁令。這意味著利蘭丁平原上展開的很可能是以劍為主、兼有長矛與騎兵衝撞的混戰，而非已經成熟的密集方陣。埃雷特里亞仍保有六十輛戰車的傳統編制，說明荷馬式的貴族作戰與城邦步兵同時存在；重裝步兵配大圓盾、青銅頭盔、脛甲，或穿亞麻布與皮革製成的胸衣，長矛之外另備短劍，盾牌的重量與形制仍在變動之中。雙方陣後也養著大量投石手與弓箭手，只是被公約排除在前線廝殺之外。此外，這場長期消耗戰把雙方的航海能力也拖進戰局：埃雷特里亞與米利都比鄰，一切糧食與徵召兵員都要靠船運，戰後期的海上護航往往決定平原上誰能撐得久。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the dory, the standard spear of the ancient Greek hoplite: about two metres of wooden shaft with a bronze butt-spike. It was not the special equipment of some elite corps but the common kit of the Greek infantryman throughout the Archaic period, with a metal blade at one end and, at the other, a spike that could be planted in the ground to brace the shield, so that dense ranks of spears could hold each other off in a collision. The Lelantine War, however, sits exactly at a turning point in that equipment, and the sources make this plain. Archilochus writes that on the day of decision the bow need not be drawn and the sling will be rare, and the sighing work will belong entirely to the sword, and that the warlike lords of Euboea were experienced in that manner of fighting; Strabo records that, when the quarrel over the plain first arose, the two cities agreed conditions for the fight, in particular forbidding the use of long-distance missiles, and a certain pillar in the Amarynthium of Eretria still carries that prohibition. The battle on the Lelantine plain was therefore most probably a mixed affair fought mainly with the sword, with spears and cavalry charges mixed in, rather than a matured phalanx. Eretria still kept the traditional establishment of 60 chariots, showing that aristocratic Homeric warfare and citizen infantry existed side by side; the heavy infantry carried the large round shield, bronze helmets and greaves, and either linen or leather corselets, carried a short sword as well as the spear, and the weight and shape of the shield was still in flux. Both sides also maintained many slingers and archers in the rear, whom the agreement simply excluded from the hand-to-hand fighting. The long war of attrition also dragged the navies of both cities into the conflict: Eretria bordered on Miletus, and every bushel of grain and every conscript had to come by sea, so that in the later stages the escorting of ships often decided who could hold out longest on the plain.
tactics: 利蘭丁戰爭的戰術可以從三條線索拼出來：公約、武器與地形。第一是公約：兩城在爭端初起時並未立刻斷絕往來，而是先立下交戰條件，核心是禁用遠程投射武器，弓與投石器不得用於決戰，只以劍與矛短兵相接，這使每一次會戰都更像決鬥而不是屠殺。第二是武器：斯巴達長矛所代表的密集矛陣在此時尚未定型，長矛仍是步兵用來格開與刺擊的個人兵器，槍尾銅套可以插地撐盾；真正大量投入的是劍，重裝步兵多靠切割而非刺穿取勝，格鬥節奏更接近阿基洛科斯筆下「嘆息的活兒歸劍去做」。第三是地形：利蘭丁平原是兩城之間一片狹長沖積地，由萊拉斯河由北向南貫流，土地肥沃，適合車馬展開與騎兵反覆衝擊縱深，卻不利於步兵方陣展開，衝突多半以小隊交鋒與單挑形式爆發。傳統記載中這場戰爭大量出現單挑場面：卡爾基斯一方的名將曾在決鬥中被一支冷箭射殺，射箭的埃雷特里亞人隨即被本城處死，因為遠程武器違反了禁用投射武器的公約，也褻瀆了兩人對決的規矩；普魯塔克記述克利奧馬科斯率色薩利騎兵打的是平原上的遭遇戰，步兵在騎兵衝撞下崩潰，騎兵反而取勝。第四是戰役節奏：戰爭很可能被切成若干階段，交戰、停戰、再交戰；埃雷特里亞英雄祠的戰士墓葬自公元前740至730年間開始使用，延續到約公元前690年，說明二十餘年的戰事在考古層面上綿延不絕；約公元前680年，埃雷特里亞人又在墓堆上建起三角形建築專門供奉陣亡者，或許正對應停戰之後的再度開戰。第五是後勤：島上耕地有限，長期戰爭必然依賴米利都等盟友的海上供應，而列夫坎迪在戰爭末期被毀，逐漸切斷埃雷特里亞與平原的陸路聯繫，逼使雙方把補給線拉長到海上。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the Lelantine War can be reconstructed from three strands: the agreement, the weapons and the terrain. First the agreement: when the quarrel first arose the two cities did not simply break off relations, but set conditions for the fight, and the core of those conditions was the exclusion of long-range missiles, no bow and no sling in the decision, the fighting to be carried out at close quarters with swords and spears, which made each engagement something closer to a duel than to a massacre. Second the weapons: the dense spear formation represented by the dory was not yet fixed in its form, and the spear remained the individual weapon with which the infantryman parried and stabbed, its bronze spike planted in the ground to support the shield; what was really thrown into the fight was the sword, and the heavy infantry won by cutting rather than by stabbing, the rhythm of the struggle matching Archilochus' line that the sighing work belongs to the sword. Third the terrain: the Lelantine plain is a long alluvial strip between the two cities, cut by the river Lelas from north to south, fertile enough for horses and wagons to deploy and for cavalry to strike repeatedly into the depth of the line, but unfavourable to the deployment of infantry formations, so that clashes mostly took the form of small bodies and single combats. Tradition records many single combats in this war: on the Chalcidian side a champion was shot down by an arrow, and the archer was in turn executed by the Eretrians because the use of a missile breached the agreement that forbade them; Plutarch describes the encounter fought by Cleomachus with the Thessalian cavalry as a clash on the plain in which the infantry broke under the charge and the horse carried the day. Fourth the rhythm of the war: it was probably divided into several phases of fighting, truce and renewed fighting; the warrior burials of the heroon of Eretria begin between 740 and 730 BC and continue to about 690 BC, which shows at the archaeological level a war running on for a generation; around 680 BC the Eretrians erected a triangular building on top of the warrior graves for the dedication of the fallen, which may well correspond to a rekindling of the war after a lull. Fifth the logistics: land on the island was limited, and a long war of this kind had to lean on seaborne supply from allies such as Miletus, while the destruction of Lefkandi in the closing years of the war gradually cut Eretria's land link to the plain and forced both sides to stretch their supply lines out to sea.
data: 關於這場戰爭，最硬的一組數字來自埃雷特里亞國勢頂峰的估算：可徵召重裝步兵約三千人、騎兵六百、戰車六十。這是全篇唯一一個傳世的城市軍力數字，恰好說明交戰時點正處在荷馬式車戰與城邦重裝步兵之間的過渡期。戰爭年代本身沒有定論：一般以公元前710至前650年為說，修昔底德的推算則把它放在公元前705年前後；埃雷特里亞英雄祠第一批戰士墓葬約在公元前740至730年間，最後一批約在公元前690年，其上建成的三角形祭所約在公元前680年。戰前關鍵的地理數字是歐里波斯海峽最窄處不足一公里，卡爾基斯與埃雷特里亞兩城直線相距不足二十公里，被爭奪的利蘭丁平原夾在兩者之間，萊拉斯河由北向南貫穿其間。殖民史的年表也提供旁證：兩城在公元前8世紀中葉合力建立阿爾米納商站，約前735年卡爾基斯在西西里建立最早殖民地尼亞索斯，同年稍後里吉翁與贊克勒在海峽兩側建立，說明戰前兩城仍在協作。戰後公元前494年埃雷特里亞派兵援米利都對抗波斯，可見島上實力已在重建；公元前490年波斯軍攻陷埃雷特里亞，是這條線索的終點。至於傷亡、俘虜與物資消耗的數字，兩城均無可信記載，只能確定這是一場歷時數十年、被修昔底德稱為最接近聯盟的大戰，其代價足以讓全島失去希臘經濟中心的地位。
dataEn: The hardest single set of figures for this war comes from the estimate of Eretria's strength at the height of its power: about 3,000 hoplites, 600 cavalrymen and 60 chariots. It is the only surviving number for the military strength of a city in the whole account, and it happens to show that the moment of the fighting lay precisely at the transition between Homeric chariot warfare and the citizen hoplite army of the polis. The date of the war itself is not settled: the usual span is 710 to 650 BC, while Thucydides' calculation puts it around 705 BC; the first warrior burials of the heroon of Eretria fall between about 740 and 730 BC and the last around 690 BC, and the triangular sanctuary built over them dates to about 680 BC. The decisive geographic figure from before the war is that the narrowest point of the Euripus strait is less than a kilometre wide, and that Chalcis and Eretria lie less than twenty kilometres apart in a straight line, with the disputed Lelantine plain squeezed between them and the river Lelas running through it from north to south. The chronology of colonization supplies corroboration: the two cities founded the trading post of Al Mina together in the middle of the 8th century BC, around 735 BC Chalcis founded Naxos, the earliest Greek colony in Sicily, and in the same year and shortly after Rhegion and Zankle were founded on the two sides of the strait, which shows the two cities still cooperating before the war. After the war, the dispatch of Eretrian troops to support Miletus against Persia in 494 BC shows that the island's strength was being rebuilt; the Persian capture of Eretria in 490 BC ends the sequence. As for casualties, prisoners and material consumption, neither city has left a credible record, and all that can be established is that this was a war lasting several decades, described by Thucydides as the closest thing to a coalition war, whose cost was enough to strip the whole island of its position as the economic centre of Greece.
cause: 關於利蘭丁戰爭為何打起來，最直接的說法是土地：利蘭丁平原由萊拉斯河滋養，土地肥沃，長期用於農耕與種葡萄。在耕地稀缺的希臘，為農業地盤開兵並不罕見，阿爾風時代的梅加拉與雅典也曾為此交兵。奇怪的是，兩城在爭端爆發前似乎已和平共用這片土地多年，究竟是何時、因何突然翻臉，古代文獻沒有交代。學者提出的第一種解釋是自然災害：公元前8世紀末，阿提卡、埃維厄與附近島嶼遭遇嚴重乾旱，歉收帶來的饑荒迫使人們爭奪每一寸可耕地，埃雷特里亞在安德羅斯的據點也可能在這場災荒中被放棄，兩城於是先後把整片平原都納入自己的版圖。第二種解釋涉及舊地盤的重新劃界：埃雷特里亞的母邦聚落列夫坎迪位於萊拉斯河口、接近今天的列夫坎迪村，公元前825年遭嚴重破壞，多數居民遷入埃雷特里亞；大約公元前700年列夫坎迪最終被毀，極可能是卡爾基斯所為，這一擊直接切斷了埃雷特里亞通往平原的通道，衝突隨即升級。第三種說法來自後世詩人提奧格尼斯的詩行，他似乎暗示公元前6世紀兩城又就利蘭丁平原再起衝突；羅賓·萊恩·福克斯因此提醒學者，不要把這樁事當成百年利蘭丁戰爭，很可能另有一場規模更小、更加模糊不清的戰爭在後面。魯賓的提醒之下，主流史學仍堅持公元前710年前後確有一場牽動廣泛的大戰存在，只是它的規模、盟友數目與確切勝負仍可爭議；德國史家德特勒夫·費林甚至主張整場戰爭是後世層層偽報堆砌而成的虛構，這一說法則未獲接受。
causeEn: The most direct account of why the Lelantine War was fought is land: the Lelantine plain is watered by the river Lelas, its soil is fertile, and for a long time it was used for farming and for vines. In a Greece short of cultivable ground, wars for agricultural territory were not unusual; in the Archaic period Megara and Athens likewise went to war over such ground. What is puzzling is that the two cities seem to have shared the plain peacefully for years before the quarrel, and the ancient sources give no account of when or why relations broke down. The first explanation offered by scholars is a natural disaster: at the end of the 8th century BC Attica, Euboea and the neighbouring islands suffered a severe drought, and the famine that followed forced men to fight for every acre of workable land, the Eretrian establishment on Andros perhaps being abandoned in the same calamity, so that each city in turn claimed the whole of the plain for itself. A second explanation concerns the redrawing of older claims: the mother settlement of Eretria at Lefkandi lay at the mouth of the Lelas near the modern village, was heavily destroyed about 825 BC, and most of its population moved to Eretria; around 700 BC Lefkandi was finally destroyed, most probably by Chalcis, and that blow cut Eretria off from the plain, after which the conflict escalated. A third account comes from the verses of the later poet Theognis, who seems to hint at a further conflict between the two cities over the plain in the 6th century BC; Robin Lane Fox accordingly warns scholars not to treat this as a hundred years' Lelantine War, since a smaller and far more obscure war may lie behind it. Even so, mainstream scholarship holds that a far-reaching war certainly took place around 710 BC, while its scale, its number of allies and its precise outcome remain disputed; the German historian Detlev Fehling has even argued that the whole war is a fiction built up from later pseudo-reports, a view that has not been accepted.
impact: 利蘭丁戰爭結束後，埃維厄島失去了它在希臘世界的領先地位。地中海市場上，歐玻亞陶器原本獨佔的份額被科林斯的瓶繪畫接手；殖民事業的頭把交椅也讓給了亞細亞岸的城邦，米利都主持東方殖民，福開亞主持西方殖民。曾經主導的卡爾基斯進入長期衰落，受埃雷特里亞管轄的基克拉澤斯諸島也紛紛獨立；反過來，兩城在戰後仍各自動手向北愛琴的卡拉基迪科斯半島移民，殖民活動並未中斷。埃雷特里亞還欠下一筆外交債：米利都曾在戰爭中站在自己這邊，因此公元前494年伊阿尼亞起義、米利都遭波斯壓迫之際，埃雷特里亞派出援軍；這份人情最終把埃雷特里亞送上不測之地，公元前490年波斯軍攻陷該城，翌年馬拉松之役中波斯再攻雅典，希臘城邦世界的命運從此被徹底改寫。從軍事史的角度看，這場漫長的消耗戰也是希臘重裝步兵體制的催生劑：在禁用遠程投射武器的公約下，劍與矛的分量上升，密集方陣的技術在長期對峙中慢慢成形；亦有學者認為，戰爭留下的城邦結盟與非正式同盟網絡，構成後來泛希臘對波斯聯盟的雛形。此外，考古層面還留下可核對的痕跡：埃雷特里亞英雄祠的戰士墓群自公元前740至730年間開始使用，到約公元前690年為止，其上約公元前680年建成的三角形祭所，是全島最早明確以軍人墓塚為核心的公共祭祀建築之一。
impactEn: When the Lelantine War ended, Euboea lost its leading position in the Greek world. On the markets of the Mediterranean, the share once monopolised by Euboean pottery passed to Corinthian figured vase painting, and the leadership in colonization passed to the cities of the Anatolian shore, with Miletus organizing the eastward movement and Phocaia the westward. Chalcis, formerly dominant, entered a long decline, and the Cycladic islands once controlled by Eretria became independent; conversely, both cities carried on colonizing the Chalcidice peninsula in the northern Aegean after the war, and colonization was not interrupted. Eretria also ran up a diplomatic debt: Miletus had stood on its side during the war, so when the Ionian Revolt broke out and Miletus came under Persian pressure in 494 BC, Eretria sent aid. That debt eventually carried Eretria into misfortune: the Persian army captured the city in 490 BC, and the following year the Persians attacked Athens at Marathon, rewriting the fortunes of the Greek city-states outright. From the point of view of military history, this long war of attrition also acted as a forcing house for the Greek hoplite system: under the agreement that excluded long-range missiles, the weight of sword and spear grew, and the technique of the dense formation took shape slowly through long stand-offs; some scholars hold that the alliances and informal networks of cities left behind by the war were the embryo of the later pan-Hellenic league against Persia. The archaeological record also leaves traces that can be checked: the group of warrior graves at the heroon of Eretria came into use between 740 and 730 BC and continued until about 690 BC, and the triangular sanctuary erected over them around 680 BC is among the earliest public cult buildings on the island built explicitly around the tombs of warriors.
result: 結局並非一場決定性的會戰。約公元前700年，卡爾基斯很可能攻毀了埃雷特里亞的母邦聚落列夫坎迪，切斷其與平原的聯繫；同一時期，埃雷特里亞的盟友米利都掃蕩了島南的卡里斯托斯，東愛琴的均勢也隨之向米利都傾斜。戰爭或許經過數次停戰才拖到公元前7世紀中葉，據說最終是在色薩利騎兵出手後由卡爾基斯取得優勢，甚至可能這場遭遇戰就是全戰的最後一幕；不過色薩利騎兵到底是否直接決定戰局、卡爾基斯是否確實全勝，古代記錄留下的空白太多，無法確定。考古上可與收尾相對應的是埃雷特里亞的英雄祭祀：戰士墓葬在約公元前690年後不再延續，約公元前680年建成的三角形建築用於祭奠陣亡英雄，說明在傳統敘事中，戰爭的代價最終以城邦自身的英雄崇拜形式被記住。戰後的希臘並未停戰：提奧格尼斯的詩暗示公元前6世紀兩城又就利蘭丁平原再起衝突，這場規模更小、更加模糊不清的戰鬥，至今仍被學者視為第二次利蘭丁戰爭，與公元前710年前後那場牽動整個希臘世界的大戰嚴格區分。縱觀全局，勝敗其實並不重要：兩城都元氣大傷，埃維厄島從希臘最活躍的經濟地區退為偏僻角落，希臘世界的注意力則整體轉向亞細亞岸的城邦、轉向地中海的殖民地。
resultEn: The war did not end in a single decisive battle. Around 700 BC Chalcis most probably destroyed the Eretrian mother settlement of Lefkandi, cutting Eretria off from the plain; at about the same time Eretria's ally Miletus ravaged Karystos in the south of the island, and the balance in the eastern Aegean tilted towards Miletus. The war, possibly interrupted by truces, dragged on into the middle of the 7th century BC, and it is said that the advantage finally went to Chalcis once the Thessalian cavalry entered the fighting, so that this encounter may even have been the last scene of the whole war; whether the Thessalian horse actually decided the outcome, and whether Chalcis indeed won, cannot be settled, because the ancient record leaves too wide a silence. On the archaeological side, what matches a conclusion is the hero cult of Eretria: the warrior burials do not continue past about 690 BC, and the triangular building raised around 680 BC was used to make offerings to the fallen, which shows that in the traditional narrative the cost of the war was finally preserved in the city's own hero cult. The Greek world did not stop fighting after the war: the verses of Theognis hint that in the 6th century BC the two cities again disputed the Lelantine plain, and that smaller and far more obscure conflict is still treated by scholars as a second Lelantine War, strictly distinguished from the great conflict around 710 BC that had set the whole Greek world at odds. On the whole the question of victory is not what matters: both cities were drained, Euboea fell back from being the most active economic region of Greece to a quiet corner, and the attention of the Greek world turned as a whole away from the Aegean towards the cities of the Anatolian coast and towards the colonies of the Mediterranean.
